label: copy-phase echo of m/u/o/p/w/a/i/d/j in long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never on original tokens or the <DEL> step, and only when the input is a fed-back token (in_first=0). Rate rises steeply with sequence length (L=9 holds 61% of mass; L<=4 almost never fires). Strongly token-selective on the fed-back input: m, u, o, p are the strongest (rate ~15-23%), then w, a, i, d, j; k, r and digits are weak. Positionally it is strongest at recall_idx 1-3 (t ~ 10-12) and again on the last copy steps of L=9 sequences (t = 16-17), with a dip at recall_idx 4-6; the largest activations are on o/u/a/p inputs at recall_idx 2 or at the final steps. Adding the position split only adds ~3 F1 points, so it is left out of the predicate. Precision is about 0.45: many copy-phase steps with these tokens in long sequences stay silent, and the rule that decides which ones fire was not found.
